Principal residence exemption when you sell

The exemption takes up to 18 mills of school operating tax off a home you own and occupy. To see it on the summer bill, you had to be both owner and resident by June 1. People who moved in between June 2 and November 1 can claim a winter exemption.

On a sale, send the Assessing Department the rescission form so the exemption ends on the correct date. A seller who has already bought another Michigan residence may keep it on the old house through a conditional rescission, as long as the old house is listed, vacant, unleased and free of business use. Submit that form with the new exemption by June 1 for both bills, or by November 1 for winter only.

Selling a Novi house with taxes owed

At closing, the title company splits the current year's tax between seller and buyer and settles any unpaid amount out of your proceeds. Get the present balance from the city treasurer. If any year has moved to Oakland County, buy an official delinquent tax statement through the county's Property Gateway, which sells them to owners and title companies.

A sale can close with tax owing, since the payoff is a line on the seller's settlement statement. The avoidable cost is the late charge: miss the winter deadline and a 3% penalty applies that staff cannot waive. Pay early, and keep both statements for the year of the sale.

A short checklist before you list: pull the summer and winter statements, confirm whether either year is past due, ask the Assessing Department whether your exemption needs a rescission form, and tell your closing agent the parcel number so the payoff figure is current on closing day. A cash sale skips the buyer's lender and appraisal, but the tax payoff still comes out of the proceeds in the same way.

Frequently asked questions

When is the winter tax deadline in Novi?

February 14. The winter statement allows payment from December 1 through February 14, and the money has to be physically in the treasurer's hands by that day. A 3% penalty starts after it, and no one at the counter can waive it.

Will a postmark count as on-time in Novi?

No. Postmarks and post-dated checks are refused. Use the drop box behind the Civic Center, pay online, or mail the check early enough to arrive on time.

Do taxes rise after buying a Novi house?

Often. The year after a sale, taxable value resets to the assessed value, which may sit well above the earlier capped figure. Later increases are limited to the inflation multiplier or 5%, whichever is smaller.

Which Novi department answers questions about my value?

The Assessing Department handles values, exemptions, and name or address changes. Bills and payments go through the Treasurer's Office at 248-347-0440.

Can a Novi house with tax behind still be sold?

Yes. The title company pays the balance, with penalty and interest, from your proceeds at closing. Request a current statement first from the city, or from the Oakland County Treasurer for earlier years.

Local schools, Oakland Community College, the Oakland Schools intermediate district, the county, county parks, the Detroit Zoo, the Art Institute and Oakland Transit all take a share. Due dates and penalties

Two bills arrive each year, a summer bill and a winter bill, and each has a payment window that closes in mid-September or mid-February. The summer bill covers school and county taxes only, so the city's own levies fall on the winter bill.

Deferment and ways to lower the bill

  • Paraplegic or quadriplegic owners.

Applicants file the city form together with a copy of their Michigan Homestead Property Tax Credit claim. The filing date moves each year, so ask Treasury for the current form and deadline. Disabled ex-service members can also ask about the exemption in MCL 211.7b, which the city links from both its tax and deferment pages.

For the amount of the bill itself, the lever is the assessment. The Assessing Department mails notices in February, and a homeowner who finds the value too steep books an appointment before the Board of Review in March. Under state law the board convenes in the second week of March, and it must send each protester a written decision, with Michigan Tax Tribunal appeal details, ahead of the first Monday of June (MCL 211.30).

Taxable value when a house sells

The buyer's taxable value resets to the state equalized value the year after the sale. A seller who has lived in the house for many years may have a much lower bill than the buyer will, and the difference is worth knowing before a listing goes up.

The city's assessing FAQ gives owners a rough way to forecast a bill: take half of the estimated property value and multiply by the current millage rate. For an addition, it suggests treating half the project cost as added taxable value.

After closing, the buyer should receive a Property Transfer Affidavit and a Principal Residence Exemption affidavit from the closing agent. Both go to the Assessors Office at City Hall, staffed on weekdays from morning to late afternoon. State law gives the buyer 45 days from the transfer to report it to the assessor.

Rochester Hills housing context

Rochester Hills became a city in 1984 and covers 32.9 square miles, bounded by Troy to the south, Auburn Hills to the west, Shelby Township in Macomb County to the east and Oakland Township to the north. The 2020 count was 76,300 residents and 31,208 housing units, of which 4.8% stood vacant.

Rochester Community Schools covers the larger share of the city, and Avondale School District covers some of the rest. The district printed on the bill sets the school millage, so check it when you compare your bill with a neighbor's. If you sell, give the buyer a copy of your most recent statement so they can see which district applies.

Selling with taxes owed

A seller behind on taxes has a practical path. Ask Treasury for the exact balance and the penalty clock, get a payoff statement from the title agent, and have the unpaid amount paid through the closing statement. If the bill has already gone to Oakland County, call the county treasurer at 248-858-0611, since the city bill carries a notice pointing owners to county hardship help.

A cash buyer does not change this. The tax payoff still comes out of your proceeds at closing, and a cash sale simply skips the lender's timeline, which can leave less room to fix a delinquency before the closing date.

Any balance still open on March 2 belongs to Oakland County, not the city, and the city's pay options no longer apply. A bill carries a notice if prior year taxes were returned delinquent, pointing the owner to the county treasurer's hardship line. Interest and penalties keep growing, so anyone selling a parcel with delinquent tax should clear it before listing or build the payoff into the closing statement.

For a deed with warranty covenants, state law has the register of deeds ask for a county treasurer certificate that no tax liens exist and that taxes for the five preceding years are paid (MCL 211.135). A quitclaim deed with no warranty is excepted from that rule. Either way, a clean tax history keeps a sale moving.

Frequently asked questions

Which number reaches the Rochester Hills assessor?

Dial 248-656-4605 for the Assessing Department. It handles values, name and address changes, and the Principal Residence Exemption. The office is at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive, inside City Hall.

What is the penalty if I miss the Rochester Hills summer deadline?

Interest of 1% attaches the day after the deadline and a further 1% attaches each month after that. The city also adds a 3% penalty after the mid-February winter deadline. Postmarks are not honored.

Does a sale change the next tax bill?

Yes. A transfer of ownership resets the taxable value to the state equalized value for the year after the sale. A buyer who inherits a long-held house can see a noticeably higher bill than the seller paid.

Can I pay my Rochester Hills tax bill by card?

Yes, online, by phone or at the Treasurer's office, with a 2.75% processing fee and a $1.50 minimum. E-check online is free. Checks go in the drop box at City Hall or by mail.

Where do delinquent Rochester Hills taxes go?

They go to the Oakland County Treasurer, 1200 N. Telegraph, Pontiac, MI 48341, from March 2. The county treasurer's number printed on the bill is 248-858-0611.

Call 734-467-3172 for tax billing or 734-467-3169 for Finance. City Hall staff are in from 9 am to 5 pm on weekdays. Values come from the Assessor's Office at the same address, phone 734-467-3160, which promises an answer within a business day.

Deeds are a different matter. They are filed with the Wayne County Register of Deeds in downtown Detroit and never at City Hall.

How is a Westland home valued for tax?

Each year the Assessor sets a value for every parcel at 50% of true cash value as of December 31, the level state law requires. The bill itself multiplies taxable value, a different figure from assessed value, by the local millage rates, so a voter-approved millage change moves the bill even if the assessment holds still.

Three appraisal methods are in use. Sales comparison looks at comparable homes that sold. The income method fits rentals. The 2026 assessments rely on sales from April 2023 through March 2025 and set aside bank sales and foreclosures as non-arm's-length deals.

A sale price cannot by itself justify a change. Neither the Assessor nor the Board of Review may raise or lower a value on price alone. The city posts its economic condition factor and land value studies, and an online lookup shows taxable value, balance owed, a parcel map and the legal description.

Contesting an assessment

The March Board of Review is the route, and it is the only time of year a residential value can be appealed. Notices arrive near the end of February, roughly two weeks before the board first sits, with hearing dates printed on them.

  • File a Petition to the Board of Review for every parcel, since incomplete ones are returned.
  • Appointments open only after notices are mailed and run five minutes each. A letter is allowed as an alternative.
  • Back your claim with an appraisal, comparable sales, a market analysis or photographs. Appointments and letters count equally, and the board decides later from the paper record.
  • Submit everything by 1:00 pm on the final scheduled meeting day.

It hears challenges to assessed value, hardship exemptions under MCL 211.7u and classification disputes, and fixes clerical errors and mutual mistakes of fact.

What if the tax stays unpaid?

The Wayne County Treasurer, at 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Detroit, takes over. A bill still open at the local office after the last day of February turns delinquent on March 1 and can be paid only to the county from then on.

At least ten written notices go out first, payment plans exist, and parcels that are foreclosed are offered to public bodies and then auctioned in September and October.

A seller with a balance can usually pay it from sale proceeds. Interest accrues monthly, so get a payoff figure from the Wayne County Treasurer before closing.

MCL 211.27a gives the buyer 45 days to tell the assessing office about the transfer on the state's form, showing the parties, the date, the real price and the parcel number. Title companies commonly hand out the form at closing.

Taxable value is limited while one owner holds the home and then resets toward assessed value the year after a transfer, so the next owner's first bill can run well above yours. Ask the Westland Assessor's Office for current forms and the status of your exemption.

Westland is a Detroit suburb roughly 18 miles west of downtown, covering 20.43 square miles of land. The Norwayne subdivision, put up for returning soldiers who worked in nearby plants, is among its oldest neighborhoods.

School assignments vary by street. Wayne-Westland Community Schools serve most of the city. The northern edge belongs to Livonia Public Schools, and small southern pockets are in Taylor and Romulus districts.

The city has 82,333 residents and 35,932 households of about 2.30 people. Housing is 61.3% owner-occupied, with a middle home value of $184,600 and median gross rent of $1,158. Median household income is $62,076.

When do Westland summer and winter taxes come due?

August 15 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter bill, after bills mailed July 1 and December 1. Council may extend either, so check the city's website for a notice.

734-467-3172, answered Monday through Friday from 9 am to 5 pm at City Hall, 36300 Warren Road. The Finance Department is at 734-467-3169.

March. Notices come near the end of February with hearing dates. You file a petition for each parcel, schedule an appointment or write a letter, and attach evidence such as an appraisal or comparable sales.

Does Westland charge extra to pay taxes by phone?

Yes, the Point and Pay line at 844-400-3556 adds a 3% service fee. Payments at the City Hall counter or in the drop boxes by check or money order carry no listed fee.

At the Wayne County Treasurer, 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Detroit. A bill unpaid at the end of February becomes delinquent on March 1 and the county alone accepts payment after that.

What are the ways to pay Wyoming taxes?

  • Online payment runs through Invoice Cloud at wyomingmi.gov/payment. Cards carry 2.7% with a $1.95 minimum, and e-checks cost $0.80.
  • Single card payments top out at $25,000, and e-checks at $125,000.
  • Accepted online: Discover, MasterCard, American Express and Visa, plus PayPal, Venmo and e-checks.
  • For mail, write the check to the City of Wyoming and enclose the stub or account number. A drop box is at the northeast entrance of City Hall.
  • Anything received after 5:00 PM counts the next day. Never mail or drop off cash.

To learn a parcel's balance before closing, call the Treasurer's Office or follow the property information link on its page.

How does Wyoming value a house for tax?

The city assesses real property at 50% of its usual selling price, as Michigan law directs. It runs a computer assisted mass appraisal system adjusted with current market data and halves true cash value to get assessed value.

The yearly calendar is public. Value notices are mailed on the last Friday of January. Complaints go to the assessor from the first Monday in February to the second Thursday, and the roll is certified on the first Monday in March. In 2026 the assessor's review closed on February 12 and the March Board of Review closed on March 12.

The city also lists every parcel by address with its current value and last sale price, in five alphabetical street ranges, so you can compare your house with neighbors before filing.

How can a Wyoming owner dispute an assessment?

Begin with the assessor's review in early February. If the answer is unsatisfying, the March Board of Review is the formal venue. Its executive session falls the day after the first Monday of March, hearings open the second Monday, and every review wraps up by the first Monday of April.

  • The board may increase, decrease or confirm a value. It can also add property left off the roll and grant poverty and principal residence exemptions that were missing last year.
  • The July and December meetings fix clerical errors and mutual mistakes of fact. The assessor adds qualified agricultural exemptions, taxable uncappings and poverty exemptions to that list.
  • The Michigan Tax Tribunal is the next step, with filing deadlines of May 31 for commercial and industrial property and July 31 for residential.

City Council appoints members to three year terms. Each set includes a real estate practitioner, a public accountant and a property owner who has been in the city at least a year.

Which other Wyoming assessing dates should an owner mark?

The assessor's calendar lists several dates beyond the March appeals. February 1 is the deadline for the qualified business form L-4143, and February 20 is the deadline for personal property statements (Form 632), small business property tax exemption claims (Form 5076) and the eligible manufacturing personal property affidavit (Form 5278).

  • First Monday in March: the assessor certifies the assessment roll.
  • Wednesday after the first Monday in April: the Board of Review roll goes to Kent County.
  • June 1: principal residence exemption affidavits for the summer bill.
  • November 1: the same affidavits for the winter bill.
  • December 31: tax day, which fixes the condition of a property for the next year's assessment.

Boards of Review judge a property by the facts that existed on tax day.

Which exemptions change when a Wyoming house is sold?

Under the principal residence exemption, an owner-occupied home is relieved of as much as 18 mills of school operating tax. A buyer must own and live in the home by June 1 to have it on the summer bill, or by November 1 for the winter bill, and a later move-in waits for the next tax year. The city says a form may have been signed at closing and that anyone unsure should file one with the Assessor's Office.

Only one such exemption is allowed per person, so the seller's old homestead needs a rescind form before a new one can be granted. Disabled veterans can claim a separate exemption using Form 5107 with Veterans Affairs paperwork, and the city asks for a copy of a driver's license.

A transfer affidavit is due from the buyer within 45 days, and Wyoming says missing it can bring back tax from the transfer date with penalties and interest. For an existing owner, taxable value is held down by the cap. A sale lifts it to assessed value the following year, so a new owner often sees a larger first bill.

What should a seller know about Wyoming itself?

After Grand Rapids, which touches it on the northeast, Wyoming is West Michigan's second largest city. It began as a farm township organized in 1848 and incorporated as a city in 1959 after annexation fights with Grand Rapids and Grandville. The 28th Street corridor, anchored by Rogers Plaza and Studio 28, became a regional shopping strip. Growth then drifted southwest to RiverTown Crossings. General Motors shut its stamping plant in 2009, and the 74 acre site, now called Site 36, is a redevelopment focus.

Census Bureau figures: 78,588 residents in the July 2025 estimate, against 76,501 in 2020, living on 24.74 square miles of land. Among 2020 to 2024 results, 67.1% of homes are owner-occupied, owned homes have a middle value of $225,200, and rent runs $1,196 at the median. There are 29,417 households of 2.61 people each, with a median income of $73,677 and a 21.9 minute average commute.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Wyoming, Michigan property tax deadlines?

August 31 for summer and February 14 for winter. Summer picks up 4% on September 1 and a half percent each month after, to a cap of 6%. Winter takes 3% on February 15.

Is there a place to pay Wyoming taxes without going inside City Hall?

Yes. A drive-up window behind City Hall is staffed Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. There is also a drop box at the northeast entrance, and online payment carries a fee.

Who gets a Wyoming tax bill after March 1?

The Kent County Treasurer collects delinquent real property tax from that date. Personal property tax stays at the city, with 1% interest each month.

When does a Wyoming owner dispute a value?

Early February for the assessor's review, then the March Board of Review, which opens hearings on the second Monday of March. Residential owners may go on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal by July 31.

Does my homestead exemption follow me from a Wyoming sale?

No. File a rescind form for the old home. The buyer applies for the exemption and qualifies by owning and occupying the house before June 1 for the summer bill or November 1 for the winter.
